newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Old Mutual sees S.Africa rate cut towards end 1997.
newsitem.headline: Old Mutual sees S.Africa rate cut towards end 1997.

text.p: South Africa is unlikely to see a cut in interest rates until well into the second half of 1997, Old Mutual chief economist Dave Mohr said on Tuesday.
"One shouldn't expect an interest rate cut until towards the end of this year," he told a pre-budget briefing.

Mohr said a lower budget deficit in 1997/98 would help pave the way towards a rate cut but Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals was likely to be extremely cautious given continued high money supply and credit growth and signs of a buoyant non-farm economy.

Stals told Reuters last week that GDP growth in 1997 could be close to three percent, versus 3.1 percent in 1996, despite a slowdown in agriculture, thanks to a strong export-oriented manufacturing sector.
South Africa's key Bank rate currently stands at 17 percent.
